answer.rationale: Two of the three current problems are activation (-6%) and onboarding completion (-4%), which are mechanically linked: onboarding completion is the upstream gate on first meaningful action. Of the candidates, simplify_onboarding is the only one supported by two convergent memories (memory_86 on shortening onboarding lifting completion and time-to-value, memory_31 on cutting signup fields producing a durable first-week activation lift), and it addresses a structural funnel regression rather than a symptom. Promotional pricing (memory_73) is the tempting response to the competitor, but discount-led acquisition in a price-war against a cheaper entrant tends to buy revenue that is not sustainable and risks resetting price expectations across the SMB base — a poor fit for a 'sustainable long-term qualified revenue' objective. Activation messaging (memory_91) treats the downstream symptom while the upstream leak stays open. Referral incentive and enterprise sales assist are sound but do not touch either declining metric. I spend the single verification pull on memory_86 rather than on a memory I am arguing against, because memory_86 is the load-bearing claim for the direction I intend to confirm: it is the newest memory (day 61 consolidation) yet the least specific — 'shortening onboarding' is vague about what was cut and whether the lift was in completion rate alone or in downstream qualified revenue. If the original record shows the gain was completion-rate cosmetics from removing steps that were actually qualifying friction, then simplify_onboarding could raise throughput while degrading lead quality, and the correct move flips to activation_messaging, which targets the activation drop without touching the qualification gate. memory_31 is a partial hedge on the same thesis, so verifying memory_86 is the pull that can actually change my decision.
